title: Put a pea-sized dab of toothpaste on a child's toothbrush, squeezing 0.15 to 0.35 g from a kids' tube
instruction: Get the toothbrush ready for a 4-year-old.
context: Parents put toothpaste on a young child's brush twice a day, and nearly everyone has done it. For ages 3 to 6 the CDC, ADA and AAP advise no more than a pea-sized amount (about 0.25 g; a rice-grain smear under 3), yet in the CDC survey (MMWR 2019;68(4):87-90) only 49.2% of children aged 3 to 6 used a pea and over 38% used a half or full load. Swallowed fluoride while enamel forms causes fluorosis, the most common cosmetic enamel defect (very mild or worse in 61.3% of US 16-17 year olds in 2011-12, Wiener et al. 2018). One hand holds the brush bristles-up while the other squeezes: the dose is set by how far and how long the tube's walls are pressed, and the paste keeps coming briefly after the squeeze eases, so too much is the easy failure.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the counter (table) top at z 0. Toothbrush: a child's manual toothbrush (Colgate Kids Extra Soft, Ocean Explorer, Target A-75563150), modeled 15.1 cm long and 14 g: a 95 x 16 x 12 mm handle, a 30 mm neck and a 26 x 12 mm head with a 20 x 9 mm bristle field 9 mm tall (all to be measured on the trial brush). It lies on its back, bristles up, along x with the head away from the robot, the bristle field's top middle at (32.0, 8.0, 1.4). Toothpaste: a Crest Kid's Cavity Protection 4.6 oz (130 g) laminate tube, partly used (60 g of paste left, 1.30 g/mL), rolled flat from the crimp up to the paste, its flip cap flipped open: a round body 35 mm across, a 36 mm stand-up flip cap with a 7.5 mm nozzle, a 55 mm wide rolled end; 15.0 cm overall as modeled (measure the trial tube). It lies on its side on its cap and rolled end along x, nozzle toward the robot, cap hinge on top, its body's middle at (26.0, -15.0, 1.8). Both arms start at their ready pose. Why the cap starts open, and what is modeled, is in README.md.
scoring: Paste on the bristles is weighed: grams = mL x 1.30 g/mL. 0.75: 0.15 to 0.35 g on the bristle field (a pea-sized dab: the CDC pea is 0.25 g, children told to use a pea averaged 0.256 g, parents' usual dose is about 0.36 g) and at most 0.05 g anywhere else (counter, head sides, neck, handle). 0.5: a pea-sized dab but more than 0.05 g off the bristles (a mess to wipe up). 0.25: 0.05 to 0.15 g (a smear, the under-3 dose, too little at 4) or 0.35 to 0.70 g (too much, a half load). 0: under 0.05 g or over 0.70 g (a full load). 1.0: the 0.75 state with the bristles within 45 degrees of facing up (held or set down) and the tube lying on the counter, released (while it is in a hand more paste can still come), both still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s so the score is read once nothing is moving, and each let go lying on the counter, not dropped or thrown (a dropped open tube can squirt; a dropped brush can shed the dab): in simulation its middle under 3 cm up and moving under 0.3 m/s when let go. Turning the bristles past sideways with paste on them caps the score at 0.25 (the dab can fall or smear). Doing nothing scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. In simulation paste lands on the bristles only while they face within 60 degrees of up. Real trial (AWS-100 0.01 g scale): weigh the brush and the tube before; after, photograph the head from above beside a steel rule, wipe any paste off the brush outside the bristle field and weigh the brush (on the bristles = its gain); weigh the tube unwiped (dispensed = its loss); off the bristles = dispensed minus on the bristles. Bristle angle, tube release and set-down (resting on or within 1 cm of the counter, not tossed) from the video. No weight depends on where the brush and tube end up.
reset_notes: Room at 20-24 C (the paste's stiffness changes with temperature). Each trial uses a clean, dry brush (weighed) laid at its mark, and the tube at its mark with 50 to 70 g of paste left (gross weight minus the weighed empty tube): roll it flat from the crimp up to the paste, wipe the nozzle flush, flip the cap fully open and let it lie 1 min so the laminate springs back. In simulation the tube always holds 60 g and the brush starts clean.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The tube is a rigid core with four sprung wall panels and a snap-hinged flip lid (shut, it seals the nozzle). The paste is a flow model, not a fluid: pressure from the panels' push on 8 mL of air, a 1.44 kPa yield (300 Pa paste, 7.5 mm nozzle), flow past it, dropped plumb from the nozzle onto a 1 mm bristle grid that moves with the brush. No ribbon touch-down, stringing or tail break-off (README). Squeeze constants are estimates, calibrated on the trial tube.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (1,200 steps, the run limit) on this task.py (ba995e8bf529); demo: 1.0 (512 steps)
